alerts.title: Abdominal pain may signal TDF toxicity
alerts.message: Guidelines list abdominal pain or discomfort and decreased appetite as presenting signs of TDF toxicity, including chronic kidney disease, acute kidney injury, Fanconi syndrome, and lactic acidosis with hepatomegaly and steatosis. Patient reports abdominal pain without fever while on TDF-containing TLD since March 2023. Evidence for drug attribution: symptom matches guideline-listed TDF toxicity signs. Evidence against: appetite is preserved, no fever, and creatinine was normal (82 umol/L) 78 days ago. Non-drug causes such as infection or other abdominal pathology should also be considered.

evidence.recommended_action: Screen for additional TDF toxicity signs (change in urine volume, back pain, fatigue, muscle cramps). Do LFTs and RFTs per guideline; if deranged, manage per toxicity algorithm.

alerts.title: TDF renal function monitoring overdue
alerts.message: Guidelines require serum creatinine and eGFR monitoring for patients on a TDF-based regimen. Patient has been on TDF since March 2023, but the most recent creatinine (82 umol/L) is from 2025-11-05, 78 days before this visit, and no renal function tests were ordered today. The clinician's plan contains no labs or orders. Although the last creatinine was normal, the new abdominal pain is a guideline-listed TDF toxicity symptom, making current renal function testing clinically indicated.

evidence.recommended_action: Order serum creatinine and eGFR now given TDF use and new abdominal pain. Continue routine TDF renal monitoring per guideline schedule.

alerts.title: Low-level viremia at 25 copies/mL
alerts.message: Guidelines emphasize monitoring low-level viremia, noting that viral load above 200 copies/mL carries risk of transmission and treatment failure, and WHO guidance supports monitoring low-level viremia. Patient's viral load of 25 copies/mL on 2025-11-05 is below the suppression threshold and indicates virologic suppression. However, this is a single recent value; ongoing adherence support and routine viral load monitoring per the adult schedule should continue to detect any upward trend.

evidence.recommended_action: Reassure patient of viral suppression. Continue routine viral load monitoring per adult schedule and reinforce adherence.
